2. Platform role and lawn-care responsibility

Mow Matter supplies software and discovery/payment tools. Mow Matter is not the lawn-care provider. Independent operators perform services, set approved prices/scope, manage workers, obtain insurance/licenses and comply with employment and safety requirements. They are not employees or agents of Mow Matter merely because they use the platform.

The lawn-service agreement is between the homeowner and the identified operator. Operators are responsible for service performance, quality, missed visits, safety, damage caused by their work, their workers and service refunds/disputes. Homeowners should contact the operator shown on their confirmed booking for field-service concerns. Mow Matter may facilitate records and communication without assuming the operator’s obligations.

To the extent permitted by law, Mow Matter does not guarantee an operator’s work or accept responsibility solely because the operator uses the software. This does not exclude liability for Mow Matter’s own actionable conduct or waive rights that cannot lawfully be excluded. Sponsored listings are paid placements, not verification, endorsement or a service guarantee. No territory exclusivity or franchise rights arise from these Terms.

Quotes may be provisional until property conditions, scope, price and capacity are confirmed. An inquiry, simulated screen or payment redirect is not itself a confirmed booking. Homeowner service scope/cadence, price, access, cancellation and refund terms must be displayed before acceptance. Additions or price changes require approval. Marketplace availability and unfinished features must be accurately described.

3. Mobile app, GPS, photos and field use

Current Crew location features use supported foreground device/browser permissions and confirmed job actions. GPS can be inaccurate or unavailable; navigation, address and safe access must be checked by the worker. Never operate the app while driving or allow a route suggestion to override safety rules. A pending offline action is not server-confirmed until synchronization succeeds.

If continuous/background on-duty tracking is introduced, the operator and crew must first receive a clear feature-specific notice and provide any legally required consent/authorization, including device permissions. Tracking must be limited to the disclosed work period, with visible status and controls. Employers remain responsible for lawful worker-monitoring policies, notice and appropriate alternatives/accommodations. These Terms do not silently activate continuous tracking or authorize off-duty surveillance. If a location-dependent feature is declined, provide the stated manual workflow where available or disclose the resulting limitation before activation.

Upload relevant work photos only where authorized; avoid unrelated people and private interiors. Never mark a job complete or upload fabricated proof without performing/confirming the work. Operators decide required proof and ensure lawful property access.

4. Intellectual property and user content

Mow Matter and its licensors own platform software, branding and product materials. Subject to these Terms and the selected plan, users receive a limited, nonexclusive right to use enabled services. Third-party software, datasets and navigation remain subject to their terms.

Users retain their rights in uploaded records, customer lists, instructions and photos, subject to others’ rights. They grant Mow Matter a limited license to host, secure, process and display that content as necessary to deliver/support the service—for example, displaying an assigned job to crew or its approved completion photo to the homeowner. This license does not transfer ownership of an operator’s customer database or grant unrestricted advertising rights. Content transfer/export follows applicable privacy obligations and the final retention policy.

Users represent they have authority for their uploads. No sensitive documents or card numbers should be placed in public inquiries. Mow Matter may remove unlawful content and restrict access proportionately while preserving records required by law.
